topic_ko: 고전 희곡·뮤지컬 대본 읽기 — 시적 형식 이해와 리브레토의 빈약함
_note: 어휘(문맥) 유형 FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab의 밑줄 어구는 해당 passage에 글자 그대로 존재. blank/insert의 target·text도 해당 passage에 존재.

passage: Classical dramatic texts, whether written by Shakespeare, Euripides, or other great playwrights, express characters' inner lives through unconventional and often poetic means.
Readers must not allow the poetic structure or archaic vocabulary to obscure the story's meaning, but should treat those features as deliberate stylistic choices.
Scripts employing elaborate language or unfamiliar conventions may demand multiple careful readings before their subtle nuances come into focus.
Reading a musical theater script presents particular challenges because the spoken dialogue is minimal while the emphasis falls heavily on song and dance.
When stripped of its music and lyrics, a musical is reduced to its bare libretto, which contains very little text.
Physical actions like dance and movement, though time-consuming on stage, can be compressed into just a few words on the page.
Understanding dramatic scripts therefore requires readers to actively reconstruct what the written words leave out.
Appreciating these genres as literary art demands both awareness of their formal conventions and tolerance for their inevitable incompleteness on the page.
choices: the historical development of musical theater from opera to Broadway
the challenges and strategies involved in reading dramatic scripts
why classical playwrights preferred poetic language over plain speech
the role of stage direction in compensating for absent music
how librettos are transformed into full theatrical productions
theme.explanation_ko: 고전 희곡과 뮤지컬 대본을 읽을 때의 어려움(시적 언어, 대화 빈약)과 독자가 취해야 할 독서 전략을 설명하는 글. '희곡 대본 읽기의 도전과 전략'인 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①뮤지컬 역사, ③고전 극작가의 언어 선택 이유, ④무대 지문의 역할, ⑤리브레토의 제작 과정은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: Reading a dramatic script is fundamentally different from reading a novel or an essay.
The poetic, archaic, or elliptical language of classical plays can create an obstacle between the reader and the story.
Rather than treating these unusual forms as barriers, readers should recognize them as tools that reveal character and mood.
Musical theater adds another layer of difficulty: the written text represents only a fraction of the total artistic experience.
With the music removed, what remains is a thin libretto that communicates very little of what an audience actually sees and hears.
Readers of scripts must therefore develop the ability to mentally fill in the missing elements.
Simply reading the words on the page is not enough; active imagination and repeated engagement are essential.
Script readers should therefore treat formal peculiarities as meaningful clues and supplement bare text with their own theatrical imagination.
choices: 희곡 대본은 소설과 동일한 방식으로 읽어야 한다.
고전 극작가들의 언어는 현대 독자에게 맞게 번역되어야 한다.
시적 형식을 방해물이 아닌 의미 있는 단서로 보고, 빈약한 텍스트를 상상력으로 보완해야 한다.
대본을 이해하기 위해서는 먼저 공연을 직접 관람해야 한다.
뮤지컬 리브레토는 음악보다 대사에 더 집중해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 희곡 대본을 읽을 때 시적 형식을 단서로 보고 빈약한 텍스트를 상상력으로 보완해야 한다는 주장. ③이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①소설과 동일한 독해 방식은 본문과 반대, ②번역 필요성은 핵심이 아니고, ④공연 관람 선행, ⑤리브레토 대사 집중은 본문과 다른 주장이다.

passage: Classical dramatic works and musical theater scripts communicate in ways that differ from ordinary prose.
Poetic language and archaic words should be read as deliberate techniques, not obstacles.
Scripts with difficult language may require several readings before their nuance becomes clear.
Musical pieces are especially hard to visualize because dialogue is minimal and songs dominate.
Stripped of music and lyrics, a musical's libretto is very thin in content.
Stage actions such as dance and movement take up little space in print but are extensive in performance.
Readers of dramatic scripts must bridge the gap between sparse text and full theatrical experience.
In short, reading scripts demands awareness of their formal conventions and imaginative reconstruction of their live dimension.
choices: 고전 희곡은 현대 독자가 이해하기 불가능할 정도로 난해하다.
뮤지컬 리브레토는 공연의 모든 요소를 충분히 담아낸다.
희곡 대본은 시적 언어의 특성을 이해하고 빈약한 텍스트를 상상력으로 보완하며 읽어야 한다.
대본 읽기는 소설 읽기보다 쉬워서 처음 읽을 때 바로 이해된다.
뮤지컬 작품은 대사가 풍부하므로 시각화하기 쉽다.
gist.explanation_ko: 희곡·뮤지컬 대본을 읽을 때 시적 언어의 특성을 인식하고 빈약한 대사를 상상력으로 채워야 한다는 것이 요지. ③이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①이해 불가능, ②리브레토가 충분히 담음, ④처음 읽어 바로 이해, ⑤뮤지컬 대사가 풍부 — 모두 본문과 어긋난다.

passage: Dramatic texts, from ancient Greek plays to modern musicals, rely on expressive forms that differ from everyday language.
A script's poetic diction and archaic phrasing are not flaws to be overcome but features to be understood.
Scripts with highly stylized language reward careful, repeated reading as layers of nuance gradually come to light.
Musical scripts are particularly thin on the page because so much of the theatrical experience exists in sound and movement.
Remove the music, and what remains of a musical is a sparse collection of dialogue known as the libretto.
A dance sequence that fills ten minutes on stage may be described in a single stage direction.
Reading a dramatic script thus requires imaginative investment that ordinary reading does not.
The page, for drama, is merely a blueprint — the building is the performance.
choices: From Page to Stage: The Playwright's Journey Through History
The Blueprint of Drama: Reading Scripts Beyond the Words on the Page
Why Musical Librettos Are the Most Important Form of Literature
How to Memorize Classical Plays Quickly and Effectively
The Death of the Script: Why Digital Theater Replaces Written Text
title.explanation_ko: 마지막 문장 'The page is merely a blueprint — the building is the performance'가 암시하듯, 대본(blueprint)을 넘어 공연 전체를 상상하며 읽어야 한다는 글의 핵심을 ②가 압축한다.
title.distractor_ko: ①극작가 역사, ③리브레토가 가장 중요한 문학, ④빠른 암기, ⑤디지털 연극이 대체 — 모두 본문 핵심과 다르다.

passage: Classical works by playwrights such as Shakespeare or Euripides contain unconventional and unrealistic methods of communicating characters' thoughts and feelings.
The reader must be mindful not to let the poetic form or archaic word usage get in the way of getting meaningful information about the story.
Scripts with complex language or unfamiliar styles may require several additional readings in order for the nuance to become clear.
Musical theater pieces are particularly difficult to visualize when reading because of the diminished emphasis on dialogue and a significant emphasis on song and dance.
When the music and lyrics are removed from a musical theater script, what is left are the dialogue, known as the book or libretto, and it can be very thin.
There is an emphasis on dance, movement, or action in musical theater that can be time-consuming when actually performed on stage.

summary.summary_template: Reading dramatic scripts requires treating __(A)__ language as a purposeful technique rather than a barrier, while recognizing that musical theater scripts are especially __(B)__ in textual content due to the dominance of song and dance.
summary.explanation_ko: (A) 고전 희곡의 시적·고어적 언어 = 'poetic', (B) 뮤지컬 대본은 내용이 매우 빈약 = 'sparse'. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 scientific/ordinary/modern이 아니라 poetic, (B)는 rich/elaborate가 아니라 sparse여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 독자는 시적 형식이나 고어 사용이 이야기에 대한 의미 있는 정보를 얻는 데 방해가 되지 않도록 유의해야 한다.
writing.answer: The reader must be mindful not to let the poetic form or archaic word usage get in the way of getting meaningful information about the story.
writing.explanation_ko: must be mindful + not to let A get in the way of B(A가 B를 방해하지 않도록). let + 목적어 + 동사원형 구조.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.

writing.explanation_ko: be difficult to V(~하기 어렵다), because of + 명사구(이유), diminished ↔ significant 대조 구조.

writing.answer: When the music and lyrics are removed from a musical theater script, what is left is the dialogue, known as the book or libretto, and it can be very thin.
writing.explanation_ko: what is left(남는 것) — 선행사 포함 명사절 주어. known as(~로 알려진) — 과거분사 수식구. thin(얇은, 빈약한) — thick의 반의어이자 문맥상 올바른 어휘.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: There is an emphasis on dance, movement, or action in musical theater that can be time-consuming when actually performed on stage, but can take very little space when typed into a play script.
writing.answer: 뮤지컬 공연에서는 실제로 무대에서 공연될 때 시간이 오래 걸릴 수 있는 춤, 움직임, 또는 행위에 중점을 두지만, 희곡 대본으로 타이핑되면 매우 적은 공간을 차지할 수 있다.
